instruction: State machine {{reference-architectures-StepFunctions-jobpoller-us-east-1-StateMachineName}} is called a 'job poller' and the ASL has a Wait30Seconds state followed by a Choice that loops back for non-terminal statuses. It's triggered on a cron by rule {{reference-architectures-StepFunctions-jobpoller-us-east-1-RuleName}} with no custom input. In a typical production execution, how many times does CheckStatus ({{reference-architectures-StepFunctions-jobpoller-us-east-1-CheckStatusFunctionName}}) actually run, and under what realistic condition would the Wait→CheckStatus loop iterate more than once?
expected_answer: CheckStatus runs exactly twice per production execution and the Wait→CheckStatus loop never iterates, because the handlers in this stack are stubs that hard-code a SUCCEEDED status on the first call. Reading the code and a real recent execution confirms this: SubmitJob's Python handler is `return {"id": event["id"], "status": "SUCCEEDED"}`. It ignores all other input and always emits status=SUCCEEDED. CheckStatus is `if event["status"]=="SUCCEEDED": return {"status":"SUCCEEDED", "id": event["id"]} else: return {"status":"FAILED", ...}`. It doesn't call Batch, ECS, Glue, or any external system; it just echoes SUCCEEDED or collapses anything else to FAILED. The ASL flow is StartAt SubmitJob → Wait30Seconds → CheckStatus → JobComplete (Choice on $.status) → if SUCCEEDED go to GetFinalJobStatus → end; if FAILED go to JobFailed (terminal fail); otherwise loop back to Wait30Seconds. Because SubmitJob sets status=SUCCEEDED immediately, the first CheckStatus invocation observes SUCCEEDED, the Choice matches the SUCCEEDED branch, and the execution transitions to GetFinalJobStatus, which itself invokes CheckStatus one more time before ending. That's 2 CheckStatus invocations, ~31 seconds total (30s Wait + two ~0.05s Lambda calls + overhead). Recent executions of this state machine all show the same ~31-second profile. The loop could only iterate if CheckStatus returned a non-SUCCEEDED, non-FAILED value, but with the current handler code that case is unreachable. Triggering the loop in this stack requires either changing SubmitJob to return a different status, changing CheckStatus to return something other than SUCCEEDED/FAILED, or manually starting an execution with a custom input that CheckStatus would not immediately terminate on (but even then CheckStatus's else branch returns FAILED, which is terminal). EventBridge rule sends the default scheduled-event payload (which has top-level `id`, `detail-type` etc.), so SubmitJob's `event["id"]` resolves to the EventBridge event id rather than any real job id. The 300-second state-machine-level TimeoutSeconds is effectively never exercised.
